abstract: We developed an ultrahigh-definition (UHD)-2/8K camera recorder that uses a complementary metal–oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensor with an organic thin-film, instead of photodiodes for the opto-electrical conversion element. The advent of UHD-2/8K Super Hi-Vision broadcasts and an increase in the production of UHD-2/8K programs across a variety of genres necessitate the development of a sensor with a good signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and high-dynamic range (HDR) to capture the full range of HDR video. To ensure successful use of this sensor, we studied the level diagrams (e.g., balancing of sensitivity, SNR, and dynamic range) that would best fit the sensor’s characteristics and use its strengths, and then proceeded accordingly. For the current UHD-2/8K location shooting, a workflow is needed to record raw data and post-process them into a practical video format. To implement a more efficient workflow, we chose to use Grass Valley HQX compression encoding while adding features that make it possible to store video data in a compressed form and simultaneously generate high-definition television (HDTV) proxy data. The workflow that we envisioned uses proxy data for offline editing and relinks them using online editing equipment.

authors.bio: Shingo Sato joined Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK), Tokyo, Japan, where he worked on the creation of news programs immediately after graduating from Waseda University, Tokyo, in 2011. In 2015, he moved to the technical management section in NHK and has been in charge of the development of camera systems for TV studios, especially for 8K, recently.
authors.name: Shingo Sato

authors.bio: Takayuki Yamashita is currently working on the research, development, and standardization of ultrahigh definition television systems as a senior research engineer with the Science and Technology Research Laboratories, NHK, Tokyo, Japan. He joined NHK in 1995 and has been engaged in research on camera systems for broadcasting since 1999. He is a member of SMPTE and the Institute of Image, Information and TelevisionEngineers (ITE).
authors.name: Takayuki Yamashita

authors.bio: Masayuki Miyazaki joined Japan NHK, Tokyo, Japan, where he worked on the creation of news programs, right after graduating from Sophia University, Tokyo, in 1994. In 2000, he moved to the technical administration section in NHK and has become responsible for facilitation planning and technology development, especially in 8K/4K production facilities, from shooting to distribution, including both package and live productions.
authors.name: Masayuki Miyazaki
